about: The company takes its leave of someone it was speaking with: how they let it go, by their manner, who the company is to them, and the hour. Not said when the company simply walks off.

lines.text: {Actor} nods, and goes back to what {they} [were|was] doing.
{Actor} watches you go for a moment, then turns away.
‘Mind how you go in the dark,’ [say|says] {actor}.
‘Come back and tell me how it goes!’ [call|calls] {actor} after you.
{Actor} has gone back to work before you have turned round.
‘Off you go, then,’ [say|says] {actor}, ‘and don’t do anything I’d be ashamed to hear about. Or do, and tell me.’
{Actor} considers the conversation over some moments before you do.
‘Don’t let me keep you,’ [say|says] {actor}, who was not trying to.
‘Be careful,’ [say|says] {actor}. ‘I know you won’t, but be careful.’
{Actor} claps you on the shoulder. ‘You know where I am.’
